# `•edge` — Edge modes

`n•edge p` gives the position on an axis of `n` items that each position in `p` reads, under the fill mode. `•edge mode` gives the function for another mode, `"clamp"`, `"wrap"`, `"reflect"` or `"symmetric"`, which takes `n` and `p` the same way. `•edge` maps over a list of mode names, as `•element` maps over tags. Like an element function, a mode function displays as the call that made it, such as `•edge"clamp"`. Positions inside the axis stay as they are in every mode.

```bpl
p←¯2+⍳8ₓ
[clamp wrap reflect symmetric]←•edge "clamp" "wrap" "reflect" "symmetric"
4•edge p         ⍝ $n $n 0 1 2 3 $n $n
4 clamp p        ⍝ [0 0 0 1 2 3 3 3]ₓ
4 wrap p         ⍝ [2 3 0 1 2 3 0 1]ₓ
4 reflect p      ⍝ [2 1 0 1 2 3 2 1]ₓ
4 symmetric p    ⍝ [1 0 0 1 2 3 3 2]ₓ
```

Fill gives 64-bit floats whatever the float pref, with NaN for a position outside the axis. The other modes give exact integers. `"reflect"` leaves out the edge item, as NumPy's and PyTorch's `reflect` do. `"symmetric"` repeats it, as NumPy's `symmetric` does. An axis of length 0 gives NaN in every mode. A NaN in `p` stays NaN.

A selection reads the positions that `•edge` gives. A NaN position reads the fill. `⌷⍠["fill":v]` reads `v` there instead. A write through a NaN position writes nothing. A position with spaces in it goes in parentheses inside brackets:

```bpl
x←10 20 30 40 ⋄ i←⍳4ₓ ⋄ clamp←•edge "clamp"
x.[(4•edge i-1)]                 ⍝ 0 10 20 30
x.[(4 clamp i-1)]                ⍝ 10 10 20 30
[(4•edge i-1)]⌷⍠["fill":¯1] x    ⍝ ¯1 10 20 30
```

Each mode is arithmetic on positions. Wrap is `n|p`, and clamp is `0⌈(n-1)⌊p`. A bare negative position counts back from the end, as in every selection.

[Windows](../glyphs/up-down-arrow.qmd) and [Stencil](../glyphs/quad-diamond.qmd) take a mode's name as the `edge` of an options record, and read their windows' positions past the ends by it, as in `["size":3 "edge":"wrap"]↕v`.

Errors: `DOMAIN` for a mode name that isn't one of the five, a length that isn't a nonnegative whole number, or a position that isn't whole.

[Dot](../glyphs/dot.qmd) and [`⌷`](../glyphs/squad.qmd) select.
